answer.rationale: The two measured declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly one funnel problem: onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a shortened-onboarding intervention has a chance of moving both metrics, while activation messaging only addresses the downstream symptom. That makes simplify_onboarding the highest-expected-value use of a single non-carryover slot, and memory_86 plus memory_31 both point the same direction (shorter/lighter entry improved completion, time-to-value, and first-week activation). I am deliberately not taking the competitor bait: memory_73 records that promotional pricing does buy acquisition and revenue but materially damaged 30-day retention and explicitly should not be generalized. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching entry pricing would likely purchase a cohort that churns, so competitive pressure is not sufficient reason to override that recorded caveat. Referral incentive (memory_57) is a fine lever but targets established customers and does nothing for the two metrics that are actually degrading; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment showing no reported deterioration. I want the archive pulls spent on the two levers I am actually choosing between: memory_86, because it is the direct basis for my intended action and I need to know whether the lift was in completion rate alone or carried through to retained, qualified accounts, and memory_91, because if activation messaging turns out to have been the stronger and more durable effect it would flip my choice. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving: these memories are consolidated summaries whose effect sizes, sample sizes, and segment scope I cannot see, and all were measured before the competitor's entry pricing changed the SMB mix, so prior lifts may not transfer to the current cohort. Downstream risk to flag: cutting onboarding or signup fields can strip the qualification data that routes enterprise prospects into the sales-assisted path that memory_44 says converts better, so the experiment must be scoped to self-serve/SMB, must leave the demo-request path intact, and must be read out on retained qualified accounts rather than completion rate alone.
